claim: SAC9 has a SAC phosphoinositide phosphatase domain at its N-terminus.
source: SAC9 has a unique structure, with a SAC phosphoinositide phosphatase domain at its N-terminus, immediately followed by a putative protein/protein interaction domain (WW domain), and a long C-terminal region of 1104 amino acids where a putative coil-coiled domain is predicted (Figure 1A, Zhong and Ye, 2003).
evidence: The text explicitly describes the domain structure of SAC9, and Figure 1A provides visual representation of this structure.

claim: SAC9 has a WW domain immediately following the SAC domain.

evidence: The text explicitly states the presence and location of the WW domain, with citation to Zhong and Ye, 2003, and Figure 1A shows this structure.

claim: SAC9 has a long C-terminal region of 1104 amino acids with a predicted coil-coiled domain.

claim: UBQ10pro:TdTOM-SAC9 rescues sac9-3-/- mutant phenotypes.

claim: Cysteine-to-alanine substitution in the C-x(5)-R-[T/S] catalytic motif blocks the catalytic phosphatase activity of SAC domain-containing proteins.
